# Valen

> Valen is a free Android app that maps training recovery down to the muscle-subzone level, upper vs. mid vs. lower chest, anterior vs. posterior delts, push vs. pull ratio, entirely from your own workout log. No wearable, no sensors, no account required. It runs on a Stimulus-Recovery-Adaptation model to show which specific muscles are actually ready to train today.

Valen is built by an independent developer, not a corporation, supplement brand, or VC-backed company. Training data stays on-device by default; encrypted cloud backup is optional and only available to Pro users.

## Key facts

- Platform: Android only (Google Play). iOS is planned but not yet available.
- Price: Free tier includes the full recovery heatmap, unlimited workout logging, exercise library with subzone mapping, and 30 days of history. Pro is $24.99/year or a $49.99 one-time lifetime purchase, and adds unlimited history, the adaptive weekly planner, deep muscle insights, encrypted cloud backup, and home-screen widgets.
- Tracks 15+ muscle subzones (not just "chest" or "back") with per-subzone fatigue that decays hour-by-hour, MEV/MAV/MRV volume targets per muscle per week, e1RM and PR tracking, and CNS strain.
- Recovery is calculated entirely from logged training, no wearable, heart rate monitor, or sleep tracker required.
- Example real-user imbalance findings the app surfaces: chest volume at 65% of weekly total vs. back at 7%; push volume running 2.2x pull volume; mid chest at 50% recovered while lower chest is at 18% recovered on the same day.
